claims.text: Design: phase 3, double-blind, 2:1, stratified by stage
claims.quote: Patients were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio, stratified by stage (IIB to IIIB vs IIIC to IV)
a personalised neoantigen vaccine (1 mg intramuscularly every 3 weeks for 9 doses) or placebo; all patients received anti-PD-1 therapy (400 mg intravenously every 6 weeks for 9 cycles)
A total of 862 patients were randomised: 575 to vaccine plus anti-PD-1 and 287 to placebo plus anti-PD-1.
Of 1204 patients who underwent screening, 342 were not randomised (insufficient tumour tissue, 201; not disease-free, 88; consent withdrawn, 53).

claims.text: RFS at 24 months, vaccine vs placebo, with HR
claims.quote: Recurrence-free survival at 24 months was 79.1% with vaccine plus anti-PD-1 and 67.0% with placebo plus anti-PD-1 (hazard ratio for recurrence or death, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.81).
Recurrence or death occurred in 128 and 98 patients, respectively (Fig. 2).

claims.text: Numbers at risk shown under the curve (from the trial's Fig. 2)

claims.quote: Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 21.4% of patients in the vaccine group and 19.5% in the placebo group. Injection-site pain occurred in 48.9% vs 9.1%, fever in 30.1% vs 6.3%, fatigue in 41.2% vs 33.8%, diarrhoea in 20.2% vs 18.8%, and pruritus in 18.4% vs 16.0%.
Overall survival data were immature (hazard ratio for death, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.52 to 1.27).
